    PortAnchor
    A fixed point that GraphArc.changeBorder() can trim a line to exactly the way it trims one to a real place or transition — used where a connection's end is not a place or a transition at all, but a port on a locked object's border, or the pointer's current position while a link is still being dragged.

    GraphCanvasModel.claim(GraphObjectFrame frame, GraphElement element)
    Claims an element for a frame, releasing whatever claimed it before - the only way an element is ever claimed, which is what makes ownership single-valued by construction rather than by every caller remembering to check.

    GraphPetriNet.paintGraphPetriNet(Graphics2D g2, Graphics g, Set<GraphElement> hiddenElements)
    Draws the net, leaving out whatever is in hiddenElements — a place or transition there is not drawn at all, and an arc is left out the moment either of its ends is, since a line to or from something not on screen would not mean anything.

    GraphObjectFrame(GraphObjectFrame other, Map<GraphElement,GraphElement> oldToNew)
    Copies another frame's own state — bounds, name, priority, template, collapsed and content-visibility — and translates its membership through oldToNew so the copy claims the corresponding NEW element instances rather than the ones other claims.
     
    GraphObjectFrame(GraphObjectFrame other, Map<GraphElement,GraphElement> oldToNew)
    Copies another frame's own state — bounds, name, priority, template, collapsed and content-visibility — and translates its membership through oldToNew so the copy claims the corresponding NEW element instances rather than the ones other claims.
     
    GraphPetriNet(GraphPetriNet graphPetriNet, Map<GraphElement,GraphElement> oldToNew)
    Copying constructor that also reports which new element replaced which old one — for a caller that holds something else pointing at the original instances (a Petri-object frame's membership, a place fusion's two halves) and needs to translate it onto this copy instead of leaving it referencing the net being copied FROM.
